title: Issue
description: Captured out-of-scope finding or drift. Source file: governance/issues.json ({"entries": [Issue]}). resolution_pointer is mandatory: issues point the agent to how to resolve without scope creep.

source.description: Who raised it — a closed vocabulary, not prose (T-0130). It was an unconstrained string and drifted into sentences like 'issue-validator sweep 2026-08-20, found while disproving I-0071', which made it useless as the 'who raises what' dimension the gate telemetry needs. 'human' absorbs the old 'user'; 'simplicity-engineer' absorbs the old 'simplicity-audit'.

summary.description: What was SEEN, at which site, and the command or observation that shows it - a summary a validator cannot reproduce from is not a report. Real examples: "harness deploy seeds no .gitignore lines for the views scrumux writes, so running a report dirties a deployed repo's tree. Repro: deploy into a git repo, commit, run scrumux views render, git status shows four untracked generated files" (I-0153); "Three walls emit wall: project-walls.conf while the four named walls emit their own names; a reader grouping by wall cannot tell which project wall fired" (I-0151). "deploy is broken" is not one: no site, no repro, nothing to confirm or refute.

resolution_pointer.description: How to resolve — the rule, skill, script, or step that fixes it, so the agent needn't improvise. It BOUNDS the work; it is not the work. Real examples: "deploy appends the ignore lines for exactly what views render writes into the target's .gitignore, once: append-only and append-if-absent, so a second deploy adds nothing" (I-0153); "The prune must never remove a path the seeding lane owns, and the exclusion must come from that lane rather than a second literal" (I-0152). "fix it" and "investigate" bound nothing, so the next session picks its own scope.

waives.description: Explicit sprint-discipline waiver list (T-0033/I-0012): only open|accepted governance issues waive, and only the tasks named here or in refs.task — never by summary prose.

evidence.description: How it was reproduced, what the run printed, and the line the mechanism sits on. Real example: "cmd-session.sh:146 tests for a .git DIRECTORY; inside a worktree .git is a file, so the stray scan is silently skipped". A disproof is written the same way and is a deliverable, not a failure (D-0011). "confirmed" is the reporter's claim restated under a second name.

validation.description: Validate-before-fix verdict (T-0034). Absent = unvalidated; hotfix promotion refuses. invalidated = close as rejected, the disproof is D-0011 data. duplicate = attach to duplicate_of and close.

validation_history.description: Superseded verdicts, oldest first, written only by issue validate --revalidate. A verdict is what both promotion gates read, so it is never replaced silently: superseding one keeps it here rather than erasing the evidence a disjoint validator recorded (F7).

authorization.description: Fix authorization on the final authority's word (I-0010). A separate fact from validation — authorized is not validated. Passes the hotfix gate on its own.

prior_resolution_pointers.description: Resolution pointers this issue previously carried, kept when --fix replaces one so a correction is visible where the wrong text used to be (T-0114/I-0057).
